title: Rotary Usage Instruction (X Series)
body_html:
This article provides an overview of the installation, configuration, and calibration procedures for using an external rotary axis on One Laser X Series, XT Series, and XRF models. The rotary axis enables cylindrical engraving, such as on tumblers, bottles, pens, and other round objects. Proper installation and calibration are essential to ensure accurate rotation and consistent engraving quality.

 

1. Prerequisites

The external rotary axis must be used together with the lifting base.
Before installing the rotary device, ensure that the lifting base has been fully assembled and secured.

 

2. Installing the Rotary Axis

Step 1: Remove the Honeycomb Panel

Remove the honeycomb bed from the working table to make room for the rotary attachment.

 

Step 2: Position the Tray and Rotary Axis

Adjust the tray height so that the laser head is approximately 3–5 cm above the surface of the workpiece.

Place the rotary axis onto the tray.

 

Step 3: Connect the Rotary Axis

Align the groove on the rotary plug with the protrusion on the machine port.
Insert the connector and tighten the securing screw to ensure a stable connection.

 

Step 4: Load and Secure the Material

Place the cylindrical material on the rotary rollers or chuck.
Turn the red knob to clamp and secure the object firmly in place.

 

Step 5: Focus the Laser

Move the laser head until the red-dot pointer aligns with the desired starting point.
Perform auto-focus, then switch on the rotary axis using the boat-style switch.

 

 

3. Using the Rotary Axis in RDWorks

RDWorks requires manual calibration to ensure the rotational steps correspond accurately to real-world motion.

Step 1: Draw a Calibration Shape

Create a square in RDWorks.

Click Download to send the test file to the machine.

Measure the engraved boundary length.

 

Step 2: Adjust the Step Value

Click Output.

Turn on Enable rotate engrave.

If the measured dimension differs from the set value:

Measured value larger than set value: Decrease the circle pulse (less rotation per step).

Measured value smaller than set value: Increase the circle pulse (more rotation per step).

Click Write.

Re-download the file to the machine for testing.

Repeat the above adjustment steps until the measured value is identical to the set value.

 

Step 3: Set Origin and Run Boundary

Upload the job, set the origin, run the frame check, and begin engraving.

 

After Use: Restore Original Settings

When rotary processing is finished:

Reopen Output.

Turn off Enable rotate engrave.

The machine display will show Starting Program.

Turn off the hardware switch that connects the rotating shaft to the machine.

Click Confirm and move on the machine display.

Wait until the laser head has completed its reset process.

 

 

4. Using the Rotary Axis in LightBurn

LightBurn provides a more guided workflow for rotary calibration.

Step 1: Enable Rotary Mode

Navigate to Laser Tools.

Select Rotary Setup.

Turn on Enable Rotary.

Input the Object Diameter in the Rotary settings.

Confirm with OK.

 

Step 2: Draw a Calibration Shape

Create a square in LightBurn.

Click Send to send the test file to the machine.

Measure the engraved boundary length.

 

Step 3: Adjust the Step Value

If the measured dimension differs from the set value:

Measured value larger than set value: Decrease the steps per rotation (less rotation per step).

Measured value smaller than set value: Increase the steps per rotation (more rotation per step).

Continue the adjustment until the measured value is identical to the set value.

 

Step 4: Start the Job

Upload the file, set the origin, run the frame boundary, and begin engraving.

 

After Use: Restore Original Settings

When rotary processing is finished:

Reopen Laser Tools - Rotary Setup.

Turn off Enable Rotary.

Confirm with OK.

The machine display will show Starting Program.

Turn off the hardware switch that connects the rotating shaft to the machine.

Click Confirm and move on the machine display.

Wait until the laser head has completed its reset process.
 

 

5. Summary

The rotary axis extends the capabilities of One Laser devices by allowing precise cylindrical engraving. Proper installation, correct focusing, and accurate calibration—especially step-value tuning in RDWorks or axis calibration in LightBurn—are essential for predictable results. Users should always restore original machine settings after rotary use to maintain normal flat-surface processing behavior.
